# firecrawl crawl

Bulk extract content from a website. Crawls pages following links up to a depth/limit.

**Prerequisite:** `crawl` requires authentication (no keyless free tier); without credentials the CLI prompts an interactive login.

## Quick start

```bash
# Crawl a docs section
firecrawl crawl "<url>" --include-paths /docs --limit 50 --wait -o .firecrawl/crawl.json

# Full crawl with depth limit
firecrawl crawl "<url>" --max-depth 3 --wait --progress -o .firecrawl/crawl.json

# Check status of a running crawl
firecrawl crawl <job-id>
```

Run `firecrawl crawl --help` for the full option list.

**Done when:** the crawl reaches a terminal status and the saved output under `.firecrawl/` contains the expected pages.

## Tips

- Use `--wait` when you need the results immediately. It has no default timeout; use `--timeout <seconds>` to bound polling. Without `--wait`, crawl returns a job ID for async polling.
- **One crawl, not a scrape loop.** If you're about to scrape a third page from the same site or section, crawl it instead with `--limit`.
- **Scope crawls with `--include-paths`** whenever the request names a section — crawl only the pages you need.
- Crawl consumes credits per page. Check `firecrawl credit-usage` before large crawls (`credit-usage` requires authentication).

## See also

- [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md) — scrape individual pages
- [firecrawl-map](../firecrawl-map/SKILL.md) — discover URLs before deciding to crawl
- [firecrawl-download](../firecrawl-download/SKILL.md) — download site to local files (uses map + scrape)
- [firecrawl-build-scrape](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills/tree/main/skills/build/firecrawl-build-scrape) — building bulk extraction into an app instead of running it here

I crawled `https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features` with a limit of 10 pages and got 10 pages back. The raw output is saved at `.firecrawl/crawl.json`.

1. **/features** – The first page returned is the SSO/SCIM page. It covers SAML or OIDC single sign-on and automatic user and group provisioning, which are enterprise features enabled per organization. The page content didn't match the base URL, so this may be a redirect or index quirk.
2. **/features/alpha/deep-research** – A legacy v1 Deep Research API that is being deprecated in favor of the Search API and the Deep Research use case. The endpoint stays active but is no longer maintained.
3. **/features/ask** – The `/support/ask` API is an AI support agent. It returns a diagnosis with actionable fix parameters in about 15–30 seconds, and it's built mainly for AI agent callers.
4. **/features/research** – A research index of about 43 million paper abstracts, mostly biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv). It has tools for searching papers, reading passages and finding related papers.
5. **/features/threat-protection** – Lets an organization block Firecrawl from fetching risky URLs. Every URL is checked against the organization's policy, whether it comes from a scrape, search, crawl or agent request.
6. **/features/llm-extract** – JSON mode extracts structured fields from a single URL with an LLM. For multiple URLs or discovery it points you to Agent.
7. **/features/crawl** – Crawl recursively discovers and scrapes every reachable subpage. It handles sitemaps, JS rendering and rate limits, supports path filters and depth limits, and returns markdown or structured data.
8. **/features/pii-redaction** – Setting `redactPII: true` on a scrape replaces personally identifiable information in the returned markdown. This is meant for data headed to agents, logs or vector stores.
9. **/features/scrape** – Scrape converts web pages into clean markdown, structured data, screenshots or HTML. It handles proxies, caching, dynamic JS content, PDFs and images.
10. **/features/agent** – `/agent` is an autonomous endpoint for when you don't know the URLs. It searches and navigates the web on its own to gather data. For a single known URL, JSON mode is cheaper.

Some of the crawled URLs have tracking-style query strings (`?m=fire573-...`) and a `#/support/...` fragment. I ignored these, and they don't affect the summaries. The summaries come from each page's opening content, not a full read of every page.
